question: task_category
instructions: Classify the user's coding-agent prompt into exactly one category based on the primary kind of work it is asking for.

planning.description: Planning, complex reasoning, architecture decisions, brainstorming, tradeoff analysis, open-ended design discussion about what to build or how. No code is being written yet, and the output is a decision or plan rather than a finished document.

coding.description: Implementing, editing, refactoring, or debugging source code; implementing a spec; fixing a bug; running/fixing tests. The deliverable is code.

research.description: Research and codebase exploration: reading existing source or docs to understand them, answering 'how does X work' or 'where is Y defined' questions. The goal is understanding, not producing a document.

writing.description: Producing or editing prose, not code: README and other Markdown/docs files, changelogs, code comments and docstrings, commit messages, PR descriptions, explanatory write-ups. The deliverable is text for humans to read. Not architecture/planning discussion (planning), not implementing or fixing code (coding), not investigating how existing code works (research).

fallback.note: Used when Jev is unavailable, low-confidence, or returns a category with no configured/available model.
